It involves the use of various algorithms and techniques to ensure that data is transmitted efficiently and reliably over a network. In this essay, we will explore the different aspects of TCP congestion control and discuss the various techniques used to achieve it.
One of the key aspects of TCP congestion control is the use of congestion avoidance algorithms. These algorithms are designed to prevent the network from becoming congested by limiting the amount of data that is transmitted at any given time. One of the most commonly used congestion avoidance algorithms is the additive increase/multiplicative decrease (AIMD) algorithm. This algorithm works by increasing the transmission rate of data when the network is not congested, and decreasing the transmission rate when the network is congested. This helps to ensure that the network is not overloaded and that data is transmitted efficiently.
Another important aspect of TCP congestion control is the use of flow control algorithms. These algorithms are designed to prevent the sender from sending data too quickly, which can cause the receiver to become overwhelmed. One of the most commonly used flow control algorithms is the sliding window algorithm. This algorithm works by allowing the sender to transmit a certain amount of data before receiving an acknowledgment from the receiver. This helps to ensure that the receiver has enough time to process the data and that the sender does not send too much data at once.
